errors: No substantive errors found. Every angle, logarithm, tabular-difference coefficient and sum checks to within the last unit of the 7th decimal.
Check of the result: substituting x = 2.1010252 + 0.8894529 i gives a residual of order 0.1 against terms of size about 700. This is consistent with 7-place logarithms.
The coefficient of x in the 7 log sin(7rho - lambda) line was overwritten in the manuscript. The correct value, -70 (= 7 × -10), is the one used: -866 = -70 - 796.

results.what: Polar-form reduction of the trinomial x^7 - 28x^4 + L e^{i lambda} = 0. The relations are r^7 = L sin(4rho - lambda)/sin 3rho and 28^7/L^3 = sin^7(7rho - lambda)/(sin^3 3rho sin^4(4rho - lambda)). This yields a single real equation for the argument rho, with the root intervals tabulated.
results.modern_name: Separation of modulus and argument for trinomial equations (Gauss's trigonometric treatment of trinomial equations)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (trinomial equations, Beiträge zur Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen, 1849/50); trinomial theory was later developed by Nekrasov, Mellin and others

results.what: Root II found numerically by linear interpolation in tabular differences of log-sines, giving rho = 22°56'41.971'', log r = 0.3582285, x = 2.1010252 + 0.8894529 i.
results.modern_name: Regula falsi / secant step using logarithm tables

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine (if virtuoso) numerical computation of one root of a specific trinomial equation, using a method Gauss is known to have used and published in outline (1849/50). Nothing here goes beyond known material.

checkable.asserts: the residual is small (|.| < 0.2), confirming root II
an exact root lies near 2.10103 + 0.88945 i
